subject: Materials Science
title: Stress and Strain: The Fundamentals
description: A fast breakdown of Stress and Strain: The Fundamentals for builders.

hook.text: Pull a rubber band and it stretches. Pull a steel wire the same way and nothing seems to happen.

buildup.text: Stress is force per unit area. Strain is the change in length divided by original length.

discovery.text: Plotting stress against strain reveals a material's personality — stiff, soft, strong, or brittle.

twist.text: A thicker wire needs more force but the same stress to stretch — stress normalizes for geometry.

climax.text: Every bridge, building, and aircraft is designed by keeping stress safely below the material's limit.

punchline.text: Stress tells you how hard atoms are being pushed apart.

quiz.question: What is engineering stress?
options: Force divided by original cross-sectional area
Change in length divided by original length
